items.headline: Putin relayed Iran's position to Trump in Friday call, offers to broker end to the war
bullets: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Saturday that Putin conveyed Iran's position on a possible resolution of the US-Iran conflict to Trump in a Friday phone call — done 'in coordination with' Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian after Putin met him twice in Turkmenistan on Thursday and offered Russia as a broker.

Terms undisclosed and Trump's response undisclosed; Kremlin says most of the call was actually about Ukraine. The White House has not confirmed the call — treat the relay as a diplomatic channel opening, not a breakthrough.

First sign Russia wants a mediator seat in this conflict — sits against Trump's fresh 'could join' rhetoric on Saudi/Houthi strikes. Watch the Sunday oil/FX open: a credible brokered channel would soften the geopolitical premium (Brent ~$104.43, DXY ~102.2); a rejection would harden it.

sources.label: Mint (Reuters/Interfax): Putin tells Trump Iran's position on peace deal
Newsmax: Kremlin: Putin Relayed Iran Peace Position to Trump

items.next: Next: whether Trump accepts the broker channel; Iran's reply on talks due within days; Sunday open in oil and FX.

items.headline: RBI opens dollar window for oil companies as rupee tests record low
bullets: Reserve Bank of India will sell dollars directly from reserves to three state oil marketers (IOCL, HPCL, BPCL) starting Monday — takes the biggest dollar buyer out of the spot market; a classic FX-defense move.
Rupee closed Friday at 96.73/USD, near May's all-time low of 96.96; the 1-month NDF rallied ~40 paise on the news in thin Saturday trade.
Also tightened currency-derivative rules: exchange-traded position limit cut $100M → $5M, no rebooking of FX derivatives, 20% risk reserve for dealers — an FX squeeze, not rate policy.

sources.label: Reuters: India central bank takes steps to support rupee, opens dollar window for oil companies

items.next: Next: does the window hold the rupee above 96.96 at Monday's open — watch spot action and the reserve-depletion cost.

items.headline: Trump: US 'could join' Saudi strikes on the Houthis; Riyadh airport toll rises
bullets: Trump told reporters Saturday the US could join Saudi strikes on the Houthis after the airport attack — a reversal from Thursday/Friday, when WSJ reported the Trump administration had declined the kingdom's plea to intervene directly; US involvement was limited to intel and targeting support for the coalition's Yemen campaign.

The strike was worse than first reported: Saudi officials say Terminals 3 AND 4 of King Khalid airport took direct missile hits, with dozens of injuries, some critical — airport closed for damage assessment; arrivals canceled across the board, inbound flights diverted to Dammam.

US kinetic entry would put the fight on two fronts (Yemen + Hormuz shipping). Watch the Sunday oil open — Brent closed Friday ~$104.43; a confirmed US strike decision would reprice the geopolitical premium.

sources.label: WSJ: Iran-Backed Houthis Hit Saudi Capital's Airport in Damaging New Attack (updated)

items.next: Next: whether Trump commits to actual strikes or holds to intel support; Sunday Brent open; any Houthi or Iranian reply to the coalition campaign.

items.headline: Houthis strike Riyadh airport again — Terminal 3 hit, evacuated; arrivals canceled
bullets: Houthi missiles hit Terminal 3 of Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Saturday: direct hit, terminal evacuated, injuries reported; arrivals canceled or delayed Saturday afternoon, inbound flights diverted to Dammam (WSJ).
Canada, Germany and Ireland warned citizens to avoid the airport — the fourth day of strikes on Saudi aviation this week, one day after the Saudi coalition's 136-target retaliation in Yemen.

The Houthis are answering the coalition's 'large-scale operation' with a capital-city strike — the tit-for-tat on airports is the live risk arc; WSJ flags the month-end FII summit in Riyadh as now in the crosshairs.

sources.label: WSJ: Iran-Backed Houthis Hit Saudi Capital's Airport in Damaging New Attack

items.next: Next: whether the coalition escalates its Yemen campaign beyond the 136 targets; and whether the 'Saudi airspace is the battlefield' doctrine extends to Aramco or shipping.

items.headline: Saudi coalition retaliates: 136 Houthi targets destroyed after the airport strikes
bullets: The Saudi-led coalition says it is carrying out a 'large-scale operation' against the Iran-backed Houthis, claiming 136 military targets destroyed — framed explicitly as retaliation for this week's Houthi missile/drone strikes on Riyadh and Abha airports (6 killed).
Parallel arc: the campaign aims to push the Houthis from the Bab el-Mandeb strait — Saudi Arabia's workaround oil-export route while Hormuz is disrupted (AP).
This was the coalition-retaliation trigger the desk was waiting for after the Riyadh strikes; the watch now is whether the Houthis answer with more airport or infrastructure strikes.

sources.label: MENA Today: Saudi-led coalition launches large-scale operation against Houthis

items.next: Next: Houthi response (more airport strikes?) and the next phase of the coalition's Yemen campaign.

items.headline: Trump re-threatens Iran at Friday rally — 'either they give us everything, or they don't exist any longer'
bullets: At a Syracuse, NY rally Friday, Trump said Iran will be 'very quick one way or the other' — 'either they give us everything, or they don't exist any longer' — and when asked about strikes before Nov 3: 'We may. I mean, we'll see.' (AP)

That undercuts his own Thursday Truth Social pledge ('we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections') — one day old; the strike-option timetable is back on the table rhetorically.

Diplomacy alive underneath: Trump calls talks 'productive'; Iran's FM says Tehran will reply to the US counterproposal within days. Rhetoric says escalation, talks say engagement — the same tension running all week.

sources.label: AP: Trump and Iran agree the election calendar isn't driving the war

items.next: Next: whether the no-strike pledge survives the weekend; US CPI Wed 8:30am ET.

items.headline: OFAC paperwork lands: General License 135 permits Russian diesel imports through April 7, 2027
bullets: OFAC General License No. 135 (dated Oct 9, signed by Director Bradley T. Smith) authorizes sale, delivery, offloading and importation of Russian-origin diesel through 12:01am EDT April 7, 2027 — the formal license behind Trump's 300k-ton diesel deal with Putin.

Narrow, not a reset: the license does not lift broader Russia sanctions, and paragraph (b) excludes debits to US accounts of the Central Bank of Russia, the National Wealth Fund and the Finance Ministry — payments must route around the blocked state institutions.
First Russian energy imports into the US since 2022 now have legal cover; the market reaction was already priced on the Truth Social announcement, so the watch is first cargoes, not more paperwork.

sources.label: Indian Economic Observer: OFAC issues licence for Russian diesel imports

items.next: Next: first Russian diesel cargo arrivals + whether Trump confirms barrels beyond the announced 4.3M-ton sequence.

items.headline: IRGC officially claims NV Sunshine strike, warns ships face 'punishment' across the region
bullets: The IRGC Navy issued a formal Friday statement: its forces struck the LPG carrier NV Sunshine (NatWit-owned) for using an 'illegal route' south of the strait — claiming a massive fire in the engine room and propulsion system. This upgrades the earlier unconfirmed claim to an official Tehran claim; still no independent verification.

Same statement claims the IRGC has 'taken control of the administration of the strait' and warns vessels on unauthorized routes will be 'pursued... and definitely punished' anywhere in the region — the formal version of the widening threat from this morning.

Separately, UKMTO confirms a distinct projectile strike ~13 nm off Al Jazeera Al Hamra, UAE (fire aboard, crew/damage unknown); Vanguard IDs the vessel as Panama-flagged crude tanker GEM NO.2. No link established between the two incidents.

sources.label: Mint: Iran claims strike on LPG tanker taking illegal route through Hormuz

items.next: Next: Sunday 5pm ET FX reopen — risk-off gap wider (JPY/CHF bid, oil up) or hold; any fresh Tehran move over the weekend.

items.headline: Iran hits Trafigura-chartered VLCC near Hormuz — strikes widening across the Gulf
bullets: Gem No 2 (302,800-dwt VLCC, Trafigura-chartered, Taiwan-owned) struck by a projectile ~13 nm off the UAE; fire on board was extinguished, crew/ship status unclear — UKMTO via TradeWinds.

Iran also claims a hit on Vietnamese VLGC NV Sunshine (not confirmed by UKMTO) and says attacks will no longer be limited to the narrow strait — widening across the Middle East Gulf and Gulf of Oman. Comes a day after the US told shippers the strait is 'open' under US protection.
Brent closed ~$104.43 (+0.55%); risk-off context into the weekend — first test is Sunday 5pm ET FX reopen.
items.next: Next: Sunday 5pm ET FX reopen — risk-off gap wider (JPY/CHF bid, oil up) or hold; any fresh Tehran move over the weekend.

items.headline: Treasury hits Iran's 'shadow fleet' — 22 vessels, 27 firms, 6 individuals designated
bullets: Numbers: Treasury (Oct 8) designated 17 shadow-fleet vessels + associated firms moving Iranian crude/petrochemicals to South and East Asia; State added 5 more ships, 10 entities, 6 individuals — framed as the biggest blow yet to Iran's illicit oil logistics ('Operation Economic Outcast').

Meaning: maximum pressure continues even as the strike option comes off the table — but the market doubts the bite: Treasury says Iran already halted loading/unloading under the blockade, and analysts say much of the flagged cargo was delivered before the sanctions hit.

FX read-through: no direct currency move — oil settled modestly higher on the no-strike news, not the sanctions (Brent $104.72, WTI $91.85). The premium that matters for the dollar stays the energy-driven inflation floor under Fed Dec-hike pricing.

sources.label: Wesal TV (Reuters): US imposes new sanctions on Iranian oil networks, 17 ships
Export Compliance Daily: US targets Iran's shadow fleet, issues license

items.next: US-Iran talks on reopening Hormuz within 7 days; Iran oil ~$104 Brent keeps the risk premium bid

items.headline: Trump strikes diesel deal with Putin — Treasury pauses Russian oil sanctions
bullets: Numbers: Trump says Russia will supply 300k tons of diesel immediately, 500k in November, 1M after — plus 3M 'within a short period' (~4.8M tons total, ≈36M barrels). Diesel fell 3% on the news; crude barely moved (WTI ~$91.20, Brent ~$104).

Meaning: U-turn just weeks after the new Russia sanctions law — Treasury issued a temporary general license, the first Russian energy imports since 2022. IEA puts the global diesel shortfall at ~1.6M b/d, so if it all materializes this plugs ~3 weeks of the gap; traders call it too little, too late.

FX read-through: mild USD relief via the fuel-inflation channel — takes pressure off the Dec-hike premium priced into the dollar, but DXY barely budged (+0.1% to 102.24). Gold +1.5% to $4,220 on the softer dollar + lower oil.

sources.label: Reuters: Trump says Russia to immediately supply 300,000 tons of diesel fuel
WSJ: Trump says he has struck deal with Putin for Russian diesel

items.next: Whether the volumes materialize (refinery-dependent); any OPEC+/Iran response before Oct 14 CPI

items.headline: U Mich misses again: 46.3 vs 47.5 — but rising inflation expectations are the real read
bullets: Numbers: Oct prelim 46.3 (fcst 47.5, Sep 48.1) — third straight monthly decline; current conditions 44.7, a record low.

Meaning: consumers gloomier, but the Fed's line item moved the wrong way — 1y inflation expectations up to 4.7% (from 4.6%), 5y to 3.5% (from 3.4%), the second straight monthly rise to the highest since May.

FX read-through: stagflationary tint — softer growth expectations argue for a softer dollar, but stickier inflation expectations keep Dec hike odds alive. Net: mild USD support via the policy channel.

sources.label: Reuters: US consumer sentiment deteriorates further in October

items.next: US CPI Wed Oct 14, 7:30am CT — the real inflation test

items.headline: Loonie sinks to 18-month low as jobs shock kills BoC hike bets
bullets: Numbers: USD/CAD 1.4275 (-0.4% Friday); touched 1.4298 intraday — weakest since April 2025; fifth straight weekly loss.
Meaning: the -68.3K jobs print keeps biting — Oct 28 hike odds down to 25% from 40%; Canada 2Y -6.8bp to 3.183%, ~161bp below the US 2Y (widest since Feb 2025).
FX read-through: market now prices BoC on hold at best — any CAD rally fights a widening rate gap. Oil softer (WTI $91.19) isn't helping.

sources.label: Reuters: Canadian dollar hits 18-month low as jobs data clips rate hike bets

items.next: Canada CPI Oct 21, then BoC decision Oct 28

bullets: Numbers: -68,300 jobs in September (consensus +9,200); unemployment 6.5% (from 6.4%); second straight monthly loss after -41,700 in August; 2026 YTD now -41,200; participation 64.8%, lowest in 29 years outside the pandemic; wages +2.3% y/y.

Meaning: losses led by public sector (education + healthcare -58,400), not tariffs — but this was the last jobs print before the Oct 28 BoC decision, and it kills the creeping December-hike pricing. Canada 2Y fell 8bp to ~3.20%.

FX read-through: USD/CAD up to ~1.4275 (from ~1.4225), near 52-week highs — the market is trading the miss. CAD's oil tailwind now fights a weak domestic story; the ~160bp US-Canada 2Y gap is the anchor.
Next: Canada CPI Oct 21, then BoC decision Oct 28.
